title: Saxton's atlas, measured
excerpt: I read 857 towns on Christopher Saxton's maps of England and Wales (1574 to 1579). A typical town is 1.4 km out, and on 31 of 34 county sheets north leans west by about 8 degrees (Cornwall excluded), close to the compass variation of the day.
seo_description: Saxton's 1579 atlas measured: towns a median 1.4 km out and north leaning 8 degrees west (Cornwall aside), like a compass.
header_alt: Title card on parchment reading Saxton's atlas, measured, in black and red, beside a detail of Saxton's hand coloured Worcestershire map, with the line 857 towns read on 35 maps of 1574 to 1579.
